label: Is the bay horse in the Colonel's colours Silver Blaze?
quote: That beast has not a white hair upon its body.

reasoning.text: Brown asked whether he should 'change it' first, and Holmes told him not to. An old horse-faker could cover the white forehead and the mottled leg, so the favourite would come out as a plain bay.

possibilities.value: another horse run in the Colonel's colours

label: Who has been backing Silver Blaze, so that his price has shortened?
quote: Somebody knows something, that is clear.

reasoning.text: Brown has the horse and has promised it shall be there. He knows it will run, and his money is on Desborough, so he has every reason to cover himself by backing Silver Blaze.
Holmes knows where the horse is and has told Ross it will start. He could be backing it himself, or through others.

possibilities.value: someone else who has heard that the horse is found

reasoning.text: News of the horse may have leaked from Mapleton, its grooms or anyone else in on the secret.

label: Who is the faker in whose hands Holmes found the horse?
quote: I found him in the hands of a faker

label: In what way was John Straker unworthy of the Colonel's confidence?
quote: John Straker was a man who was entirely unworthy of your confidence

possibilities.value: he meant to lame the favourite himself

reasoning.text: The horse killed him in self-defence, so Straker was attacking it. He had an uncorked cataract knife and had struck a light in the hollow, and the sheep in his paddock were lamed.

possibilities.value: he kept a costly second life under the name of Derbyshire

reasoning.text: A Bond Street bill made out to 'Derbyshire' was in his pocket, and his wife never had such a dress.

possibilities.value: he had money on the race against his own horse

reasoning.text: A trainer who lames his own favourite would profit only by betting against it, perhaps to pay for that second life.
In the owners' enclosure Holmes has only Watson, the Colonel and the horse with him. The Colonel was the trainer's master and has been cold throughout.

value: the horse killed the trainer, who was harming it, and then ran loose
nobody meant to carry him off: he was led out to be harmed and got loose

reasoning.text: If the horse killed Straker in self-defence, Straker led it out to do something to it. The horse then ran off by itself and was taken up later at Mapleton.
